title: Decide how sub-agent tool calls hold a turn: blocking lease or parked gate
description:
**Design question raised 2026-09-17: we plan to support tool calls that are sub-agents, which recursively call further tools and agents. Those can run for hours.**

`65b431` makes minutes safe by renewing the lease during tool execution. It does not make hours safe, and holding a lease for hours is the wrong shape:

- The parent worker is pinned for the whole duration doing nothing but renewing.
- If the parent crashes, the lease lapses and the turn is reclaimed even though the sub-agent is still working.
- The lease stops meaning "this worker is alive" and starts standing in for "something somewhere is alive," which is not what the watchdog checks.

The codebase already has the better shape. `_escalate_file_tool` (`worker/computerless.py`) hands work to the computer host, and `emit_turn_waiting` (`control_plane.py:3331`) parks the turn on a named gate. The watchdog explicitly tolerates that state — `if turn.waiting_for is not None: reschedule; return` (`control_plane.py:3237`) — so a parked turn is never reclaimed, however long the gate takes.

## The question to settle

Should a sub-agent tool call be modelled as a blocking call the parent makes, or as another unit of work that reports back through a gate?

The second is what the escalation path already does for host tools, and it removes the duration problem entirely rather than raising a limit. It also gives recursion somewhere sensible to live: a sub-agent's own turn can park on its own gates without its parent holding anything.

Costs to weigh honestly: a gate needs a resumption path (`resume_waiting_turn` exists at `control_plane.py:3365`), nested turns need their spend attributed to the right org, and cancellation has to propagate down the tree. None of that is free, and a blocking call with a renewed lease is genuinely simpler for shallow cases.

## Not a decision to make from the code alone

This wants a human call on the model before implementation. Recording the shape and the evidence so the decision is made deliberately rather than by whichever path is easiest at the time.

## Done when

The model is decided and written down, with the resumption, attribution, and cancellation consequences stated.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
This should be answered before `65b431`, not after. I originally sequenced them the other way round.

Checked what runs inline today: `dispatch_gated_tool` handles only `browse`, and only to authorize a URL. Every other tool is denied. So there is no long inline tool call to protect yet, and `65b431` is currently unreachable rather than urgent.

That makes this card the deciding one. If sub-agents run as inline blocking calls, `65b431` becomes a prerequisite and lease renewal has to cover arbitrarily long work. If they park on a gate — the shape `_escalate_file_tool` and `emit_turn_waiting` already use — inline calls stay short, `65b431` stays a small latent fix, and the duration problem does not exist rather than being raised.

The answer here determines the priority of the other two cards, so it is worth settling deliberately rather than discovering by implementation.
